why:
ours is the named constructor `QoS::sensor_data()`. rclcpp gives each QoS preset its own TYPE so a preset can be passed where a `QoS` is expected and still be named; ours are named constructors on one `QoS`. See the service stage's `cpp:ServicesQoS::ServicesQoS`. COLLAPSE CHECK 2026-09-04 (phase-417): the "a type per preset costs a class each with no allocator to justify it" argument NO LONGER HOLDS. phase-417 W3.f ships `SensorDataQoS`, `ServicesQoS`, `ParametersQoS`, `ParameterEventsQoS`, `RosoutQoS` and `ClockQoS` as `constexpr` classes deriving from `QoS` in `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/qos.hpp:703`–`:751` (in `rclcpp_compat.hpp` until phase-417 stage 6 step A deleted it), transcribed field-for-field from `rmw/qos_profiles.h`, with no allocator involved -- so this correlates `same` on the PORTED surface. The row survives because `--check` gates the NATIVE bucket, where this is still `theirs-only`: `nros::QoS` still spells the presets as named constructors (`qos.hpp:328-334`) and ships only three of them.

phase-428 W6 (2026-09-06) — disposition, required because this row's SHAPE CORRESPONDS: the name exists on the ported surface and the correlator files it `same`, so nothing in a build says the contract differs. That is the class RFC-0089 exists for.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp::SensorDataQoS` is `QoSInitialization::from_rmw(rmw_qos_profile_sensor_data)` — a REFERENCE to the rmw constant, never a re-transcription of it (`rclcpp/qos.hpp:391-399`).

OURS: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/qos.hpp:703` — a `constexpr class SensorDataQoS : public QoS` whose entire content is the matching row of `nros::detail::qos_table`, the phase-428 W10 SSoT. The values are pinned by `static_assert` in `tests/compile/ros2_api_adoption_stage2.cpp` rather than by review, because two siblings shipped WRONG: `ParametersQoS()` returned depth 10 against upstream's 1000, and `SystemDefaultsQoS()` returned a DIFFERENT upstream profile and is now REFUSE-LOUD.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: there is nothing to find out — the name, the base class, the brace and paren spellings and the ten policy values are upstream's, and a test says so on every build of the compile lane.

THE BOUNDARY OF THIS CLAIM, stated because `adopt` is a strong word: it is about the PROFILE this name denotes, not about which policies a backend then honours. Whether a request for a depth the ring cannot hold is honoured, downgraded or refused is phase-428 W9's work item, and it applies identically to a hand-written `nros::QoS` — it is not a property of this name.
